children: Brazil's central bank and the national monetary council announced on Wednesday new measures to contain household indebtedness in the country, including restrictions on unsecured lending and reduction in credit card limits for some customers with overdue debt.

"These initiatives seek to strengthen safeguards against the buildup of vulnerabilities associated with indebtedness," the central bank said in a statement, adding most of the new rules will take effect on July 1 next year.
